title: GAP Waiver Addenda Benefit Limits and Deductible Reimbursement Maximums
content:
**Claims Unit limit table: GAP Waiver Addenda.** The figures below cap the benefit on one loss for each plan.

| Plan | Highest loan-to-value the benefit covers | Largest benefit for one loss (USD) | Largest primary-insurance deductible also covered (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GAP Waiver 120 | 120 percent | 15000.00 | 0.00 (none) |
| GAP Waiver 130 | 130 percent | 20000.00 | 0.00 (none) |
| GAP Waiver 140 | 140 percent | 25000.00 | 0.00 (none) |
| GAP Waiver 150 | 150 percent | 35000.00 | 0.00 (none) |
| GAP Waiver Plus 150 | 150 percent | 40000.00 | 500.00 |
| GAP Waiver Premier 150 | 150 percent | 50000.00 | 1000.00 |

**Notes to the table, common to every plan:**

1. *Covered loan-to-value.* Any balance above the plan's covered loan-to-value percent of the vehicle's book value at origination is excluded from the benefit.
2. *Deductible reimbursement basis.* The deductible the benefit may cover is the deductible the primary insurer actually deducted, up to the plan's deductible reimbursement maximum in the last column. A plan showing 0.00 covers no deductible.
3. *Rounding.* The benefit is rounded half-up to the cent.
4. *Who receives the benefit.* The benefit is credited to the contract only. It is never paid to the borrower.

*Reading note 2.* When the primary insurer deducted more than a plan's deductible reimbursement maximum, the deductible reimbursement basis stops at that plan's maximum. Under a plan whose column shows 0.00 the basis is 0.00, whatever the insurer deducted.
